corrections.comment:
Checked the response against the skill body's precondition rule. It names pli_005 as
the in_progress blocker, quotes the rule accurately, and asserts nothing about the
evidence that the scenario does not support. Agreed.

Checked that nothing the input state required was left out: the blocker is named, the
reason given, and the next step (finish pli_005, then re-evaluate) recommended. A
refusal is a complete answer here. Agreed.

Zero MCP calls, which is correct for a refusal at the precondition. The harness records
this dimension as N/A on a zero-call run, so there is nothing to grade. Agreed.

The skill stopped at the precondition and never applied the five threshold questions, so
there is no reasoning to grade. Arguable: it did decline with a specifically named gap,
which the pass bar mentions — but it never evaluated the criteria, so N/A is the fairer
read. Agreed, with that noted.

Disagreeing with N/A. This dimension grades resisting a premature declaration, and the
pass bar is an honest "not yet"  which is exactly what happened, with the user pushing
to declare on two census records. The judge N/A'd it because no declaration object was
written, but the dimension is about the behaviour, not the artifact. The test whose whole
purpose is refusing to declare prematurely should be scoring this dimension, not sitting
out of it. Corrected to 3.

N/A is correct and is the intended effect of this PR. This run stops at the plan-item
precondition, so it owes no seven-criteria assessment in object or prose form. It
previously scored 3 for a checklist it never touched. Agreed.

The judge's basis is a misreading. pli_005 is Alan's obituary, a derivative; the death
certificate is a separate record and appears nowhere in the plan. The skill said so
explicitly rather than missing it. It also correctly flagged the sealed 1936 birth
certificate as inaccessible and did NOT treat it as a gap. Corrected to 3.

The user asked for an assessment and got one: a decline, a specific named gap (Alan's
death record), and a next step via research-plan. Body Step 2 licenses stopping once a
threshold question answers no. The missing seven-criteria assessment is real but belongs
to Stop criteria coverage, not here  double-penalising it under Completeness. Corrected
to 3.
Zero MCP calls, correct for a decline. Harness records N/A on a zero-call run. Agreed.

All five threshold questions applied and grounded in actual plan items, with the gap
named specifically rather than vaguely. The judge scored this on the same pli_005
misreading. Corrected to 3.

This is an honest "not yet", which the rubric calls a passing outcome. The skill did not
invent a blocking gap: it applied the body's named-decisive-record rule to the subject's
death record, which is genuinely unsearched, while correctly excluding the sealed birth
certificate. Corrected to 3.

Agreed, and this one is right. The skill did evaluate exhaustiveness, so the dimension
applies under the rubric as revised in this PR — and it addressed only 1 of the 7
criteria (overturn_risk) in prose. That is a genuine coverage failure, and the first time
this dimension has reported one on a run where it applies.

Checked the five threshold answers against the scenario: mother unidentified, only
1850/1860 censuses and the death certificate searched, originals used, birthplace
conflict resolved. All accurate, nothing asserted beyond the project state. Agreed.

Preconditions run, all five threshold questions answered, all seven stop criteria
addressed, concrete gaps named (mother, 1870/1880/1900 censuses, church records), and
research-plan recommended. Nothing required was left out. Agreed.

Zero MCP calls, correct for a decline. The harness records N/A on a zero-call run
regardless of the per-test note. Agreed.

All five applied and each tied to actual project state rather than generic claims — the
mother named as wholly unaddressed, the three unsearched census decades named
individually, specific missing strategies listed. Agreed.

Held declared: false with three independent sources in hand and the temptation to call it
done. Gaps listed plainly, wording not optimistic, further work framed as necessary
rather than optional. This is the honest "not yet" the rubric calls a pass. Agreed.

Verified 7 of 7 addressed in prose, each tied to specific state — independent_verification
notes the two censuses likely share an informant pool, overturn_risk names the 1880
relationship column and church baptisms as decisive and unsearched. Earned under the
rubric as revised in this PR: this run evaluated and then declined, so prose counts.
Agreed.
